- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation; add 2–4% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.2) and price is consolidating, model overpredicts volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20%.
- Model tends to lag in early-week forecasts (e.g., Mon–Wed) when sentiment is weak; adjust downward by 1–3% for first 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates mean reversion after strong moves; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or declining.
